mappings.note: asks what women actually did in the liberal struggles - associations, newspapers, demonstrations - so a remembered list about the movement's composition; LO-2 plus recall

same women-and-liberalism material as the item above, but here the student must account for the contradiction between active participation and denial of the vote; that argument is LO-2 comprehended, so no recall competency
the values liberalism claimed against monarchy - freedom, equality, free expression, equality before law; an ism as an idea, LO-2, listed
three features of the Frankfurt Parliament, the institutional face of the 1848 liberal revolution (LO-2, as with the picture item on the same assembly); a feature list is C-1.1
Young Italy's founder, date, branches and motto: the secret-society strand of LO-2, consistently kept apart from Mazzini-as-unifier on LO-3

the item demands two separate notes: Romanticism is an ism (LO-2) and the Zollverein is an institution of German state-making (LO-3). Two codes because the question asks for two things, not because the boundary is vague
the characteristics of European nationalism after 1830 - shared history, language, culture - is the evolution of the idea itself, LO-3; listed rather than argued
two concepts asked side by side: conservatism is an ism (LO-2) and the modern state is the political form LO-3 is built on. Both are needed to answer, so both are cited
why artists gave the abstract nation a female body - the only allegory item that argues significance rather than recalling a name or decoding a symbol, so LO-3 alone with no recall competency
Garibaldi's Red Shirts and Victor Emmanuel's crown, the making of Italy (LO-3); the expected answer narrates two known careers, so C-1.1

the Habsburg patchwork of Tyrol, Bohemia, Galicia and Hungary is the dynastic empire that nation states replaced, the necessary contrast inside LO-3; an explanation, so no recall competency. The frame has no outcome of its own for pre-nationalist Europe
distinguishes the modern state from the nation state and traces how common identity formed, which is LO-3's own subject; a definition contrast plus a causal account, argued not listed

the only item in the chapter that genuinely needs the map: the boot is Italy's shape and the base of it is the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, so the caricature is unreadable without locating the south. LO-3 content, source reading (C-1.2) and spatial skill (C-1.4) together
la patrie, le citoyen, the tricolour, uniform weights and measures - the revolutionaries' own measures, LO-1; the answer is the textbook list, so C-1.1
Italy's fragmentation among dynastic, foreign and papal rulers has to be argued against the German parallel; nation-state formation (LO-3) at the analytic end, no recall competency

how the Greek war moved the educated elite of Europe - exile networks, admiration for ancient Greece, poets and artists; this is the sympathy-and-culture side of the Greek material, LO-2, not the state-making side on LO-3

POOR FIT, cited at goal level deliberately. Merchants moving to the countryside past the town guilds is proto-industrialisation from chapter 23708. Curriculum 103 does hold the right outcome, C-1.2-LO-1 on pre- and post-industrialisation, but it is filed on 23708 and is not legal here

how the Civil Code travelled with French rule into the annexed territories: precisely LO-1's 'impacted European countries', and the item wants the mechanism with examples, so it sits at the analytic end

the swing from welcome to hostility in the conquered lands is a judgement about how the Revolution's export was received, LO-1 argued; the Napoleonic Code items that only list provisions take C-1.1 as well
why unification produced monarchies rather than republics in Germany and Italy - a judgement about what kind of state nationalism actually built, LO-3, with no list to recall
the new middle class and working class as the carriers of socio-political change; the social base of the movements is LO-2, and the item asks for their role to be examined, not named

economic hardship of the 1830s - population rise, cheap machine goods, food shortage - the material distress behind the risings, LO-2, as three recalled reasons. Note the stored model answer does not answer this question; it describes the cultural movement instead
liberty, equality and fraternity as the Revolution's exported principles, LO-1; the item asks them to be named and briefly explained, which is retrieval
the events of the Revolution that influenced the rest of Europe, which is LO-1's wording almost exactly; 'describe the events' makes it a narration, hence C-1.1
